notes: v1.14.579 — THE BLOCKERS KPI STOPS COUNTING WHAT IT CANNOT KNOW. Fix for the .578 cold-launch FAIL on a fresh device, ruled by the owner. THE DEFECT: on a phone with no Master and no deployment, the Command hero's Blockers cell rendered a counted "0". A zero reads as "none open, all clear"; the truth was "there is no deployment, so the question has no answer". .577 and .578 fixed exactly this lie on the readiness row and on the stat row and never reached the hero, because the hero is a DIFFERENT RENDERER with no dot vocabulary and no na class. Three surfaces, one concept, and the fix had landed on two of them. THE TREATMENT IS THE .578 TREATMENT, PORTED. One class, .cs-kpi.na, carries opacity AND number colour together, so this cell cannot end up half-styled the way the readiness row did at .577. The cell reads an em dash, slate and muted, whenever there is no active deployment. NO DOT WAS ADDED, AND THAT IS THE RULING. A .cs-hdot on this card would have inherited the default green fill and green glow, putting a lit pass-signal on the KPI whenever a deployment existed — the .577 defect reproduced on a fourth surface. The KPI row has no dot vocabulary to join, so the honest treatment is the muted number the stat row already uses. THE COUNT NOW COMES FROM THE ACTIVE DEPLOYMENT ONLY. The aggregate blockerCount sums EVERY deployment, so the cell could report blockers the hero's own headline was not about. Aggregate counts never drive this cell; the param is left deliberately unread. That also closes a latent contradiction — the aggregate could set .hot with no active deployment, so na and hot could co-exist on one cell. FOUND ON A COLD LAUNCH, NOT BY A TEST. Every .578 assertion passed and still passes; the surface had no coverage. 98-cmd-census.spec.js gains it.
